leads.leadLine: Smartwatches and symptom tracking in ENDO1000
leads.reason: ENDO1000 combines wearable measurements with repeated symptom reports. That makes this team a concrete place to explore independent validation of WombWise's wearable signals.
leads.ask: Ask whether a separately agreed validation study could compare WombWise's signals with longitudinal symptom measures. ENDO1000 already has its own app; establish what collaboration could add.

leads.name: Oxford EndoCaRe & reproductive health
facilities: Nuffield Department Women's and Reproductive Health

siteStatuses.facility: Nuffield Department Women's and Reproductive Health

leads.leadLine: Prospective pain-outcome research and an enquiry desk
leads.reason: Oxford's registered study follows pain outcomes around endometriosis surgery. Its research centre also publishes a general enquiry route, so there is a clear starting point for a validation discussion.
leads.ask: Ask the EndoCaRe team whether passive wearable measures would answer a useful question alongside their existing pain-outcome research.

leads.leadLine: Endometriosis studies with a verified NHS research route
leads.reason: The Trust appears in recent endometriosis study records. Its research office explicitly supports outside researchers and sponsors with feasibility and study setup.

leads.reason: DAISy-PCOS brings together clinical phenotyping and metabolic measurements. Birmingham publishes a business route for collaborative research, which could connect WombWise to the relevant PCOS investigators.
leads.ask: Ask the business engagement team for an introduction to PCOS researchers interested in evaluating wearable signals alongside clinical phenotyping.
